subject: Science
title: Cells and genetics check
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 6.87 on 1001 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 12.87 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: I am learning to use cell and inheritance models to show what I know and choose one next step.
success_criteria: I can order copy, separate and split for mitosis.
I can mark one gene as part of DNA.
I can use a simple cross as probability, not a promise.

vocab.definition: division of the nucleus to separate matching chromosome sets
vocab.example: Mitosis helps make matching body cells.

vocab.definition: a section of DNA that codes for a protein
vocab.example: A gene is a part of the DNA string.
A and a stand for two alleles in our invented model.

vocab.definition: a fact or model detail that supports a claim
vocab.example: The labelled chromosome sets are evidence for my answer.

worked_example.full: Parallel example (not one of the check items): label a body-cell model with copied chromosome sets, then explain that mitosis separates them into two nuclei. Point to a model detail that supports the answer. Now cover the labels for the independent check.
worked_example.faded: Parallel example: the chromosome sets are copied. Mitosis moves the sets to ___ nuclei; the evidence detail is ___.
worked_example.removed_step: State that matching chromosome sets go into two nuclei and cite a labelled detail.
worked_example.fade_next: At the following review, remove the example’s sentence stem and invite an independent evidence explanation.

cfu.question: Show me: does “describe” need a model detail or a personal story?

hinge.question: Which paired statement is scientifically accurate?

options.text: A. Mitosis halves chromosome number; a gene is the whole genome.
options.diagnosis: Confuses mitosis with meiosis and gene with genome.

options.text: B. Mitosis removes DNA; an allele is a separate cell.
options.diagnosis: Treats DNA as used up and allele as a cell.

options.text: C. Mitosis makes one unsplit cell; DNA is only in proteins.
options.diagnosis: Misses cell splitting and confuses DNA with protein.

options.text: D. Mitosis gives matching body cells; a gene is a section of DNA.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → begin the check. Otherwise re-model a two-colour copy/separate/split strip and a short gene mark on a DNA string, then ask the parallel hinge. Do not pre-answer the three check items.
hinge.parallel_hinge: What shows a gene on our string model? A. A marked section of the DNA string (expected). B. The whole organism. C. A cell outside DNA. D. An empty grid square.

misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses A, the halving claim.
misconceptions.correction: Use a separate two-colour strip to show copying and matching sets; do not coach the assessment response.

misconceptions.misconception: A gene is the whole genome.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses A, calling a gene the whole genome.
misconceptions.correction: Show a short mark on a separate DNA string, then leave the check item unsupported.

we_do.support: Use command words and a different model first; put it aside before independent items.
we_do.stretch: Give a limit of the rehearsal model: a diagram shows order but not every molecular step.

tiers.F: In the independent check, order the three stages and mark one gene on the model.
tiers.M: Explain matching body cells and why a gene is only part of DNA.
tiers.H: Use Aa × aa to reject the claim that a probability promises an exact family count.

stems.H: The model chance is …; the real count may differ because …

tiers.go_deeper: Which model feature supports an explanation that transfers to a fresh example, and which detail is only the model?
tiers.early_finisher: After submitting the check, compare two wrong cross explanations. Name each misconception and a precise repair without altering the checked answer.

adaptations.cognition_learning: Keep the cell and allele model in view; remove one cue for We do, then ask pupils to repeat a fresh example without it.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Offer the key word card and a private partner turn before speaking to the group; accept point, sign or AAC.
adaptations.semh: Check in before the top question and hinge; offer a private first answer, agreed pause and one-step return.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Provide an enlarged high-contrast model and keyboard focus; allow speech-to-text or exact scribing.
adaptations.eal: Pre-teach defined science words with examples; let pupils plan in any language while keeping M/H reasoning open.

speaking_frames: This model shows …; the detail I used is …
My answer is … because the labelled model shows …

ta_focus.i_do: “Watch how I use a different model detail in my answer.”
ta_focus.we_do: “Which detail can you point to as evidence?”
ta_focus.independent: “Read the command. Choose one valid response mode; this item is yours.”

prompt_ladder: Wait five seconds for a self-start with command words.
Point to the command word, not the answer location.
Ask “Which item are you on?” without hinting at content.
Model a parallel non-test item only; pupil then returns to a fresh check item.
Correct the procedure (for example, which box to use), never a test answer.

F.q: Which step copies DNA before mitosis?
Is a gene part of DNA or a whole cell?

M.q: Why can two body cells match after division?
M.a: Copied chromosome sets separated into two new cells.

H.q: In Aa × aa, what does two aa squares out of four mean?
H.a: A model chance of one in two, not an exact family count.

H.q: Which diagram detail would you cite for a gene claim?
H.a: The marked DNA section, not the full chromosome.

interactions.answer_key: D. Mitosis gives matching body cells; a gene is a section of DNA. Teacher reads group response; no automatic grade.
